stages.name: Unfold
stages.text: The arm unfolds. Gel and water stand at the same level (87 mm); the mouth of the head is open down to the floor.

stages.name: Kit
stages.text: The kit is seated on the floor of the bowl; the print wraps it.

stages.name: Tool change
stages.text: Holder off, print needle on; every move stays in the tail, as in the fertile build.

stages.name: Print
stages.text: The print needle lays the newborn at its final size, folded, as a quilt of 9 hoop cells: laid flat in two layers, folded in 3 panels across and 3 along on the seams, 18 layers, 128 x 187 x 79 mm, 1154 mL of Dragon Skin 30.

stages.name: Cure, change
stages.text: Cure in the gel (Dragon Skin 30, 16 h at room temperature, maker's bulletin). Tool change back to the holder.

stages.name: Push out
stages.text: The interlayer is still full of gel and flat: the body passes the 201 mm wide open mouth folded. The holder pushes it 165 mm, until its rear face is 5 mm past the mouth plane.

stages.name: Clear and inflate
stages.text: Gel out of the interlayer (419 mL, plug push 0.16 kPa at 9 Pa), then air to 13.6 kPa: 5.7 L in 55 s. The interior stays open to the water.

stages.name: Release
stages.text: The line pulls out of the valve, which closes; the arm folds into the tail.

stages.name: Swim into the lane
stages.text: Turning radius about 120 mm on the off axis outlet (fertile build, estimate); speed about 49 mm/s on the 39 mN jet (estimate).

stages.name: Release, back off
stages.text: One Pololu 298:1 gearmotor winds a cord that tilts the seam magnets about their edges: 12.8 N each against 54 N straight off. The gel faces open; gel and water stand level, so they hold.

stages.name: The tail comes round
stages.text: Two wheels: back off 80 mm, a quarter turn, 385 mm across, a quarter turn back, 757 mm forward; contact at the newborn's cuff. In 87 mm of water the tail is lighter: about 2.6 N on the wheels (fertile build 12 N).

stages.name: Dock
stages.text: Nine pairs, 172 to 343 N, against 16.7 N of push with the safety factor; the rim spans 125 mm between pairs. The newborn is the head now.

stages.name: Gel into the soft head
stages.text: About 5.2 L of gel to the water level, at 0.1 L/min; the soft head keeps its shape, as nothing presses on its walls: gel and water stand level.

stages.name: Kit (generation 2)
stages.text: Same moves as in the hard head: the inner face of the soft head is the inner face of the hard head.

stages.name: Tool change (generation 2)
stages.text: Holder off, print needle on.

stages.name: Print (generation 2)
stages.text: The print needle lays the newborn at its final size, folded, as a quilt of 9 hoop cells: laid flat in two layers, folded in 3 panels across and 3 along on the seams, 18 layers, 128 x 187 x 79 mm, 1154 mL of Dragon Skin 30.

stages.name: Cure, change (generation 2)
stages.text: Cure; tool change.

stages.name: Push out (generation 2)
stages.text: The interlayer is still full of gel and flat: the body passes the 201 mm wide open mouth folded. The holder pushes it 165 mm, until its rear face is 5 mm past the mouth plane.

stages.name: Clear and inflate (generation 2)
stages.text: Gel out of the interlayer (419 mL, plug push 0.16 kPa at 9 Pa), then air to 13.6 kPa: 5.7 L in 55 s. The interior stays open to the water.

stages.name: Born; the soft head stands
stages.text: The soft head kept its shape through the birth: its interior was never under pressure, its quilt held 13.6 kPa throughout, fed through the nipple.

The print cures in the gel (Dragon Skin 30: 16 h). The needle goes back, the holder comes on.
The holder's ball needle (two lumen) goes into the valve at the top of the rear face of the folded body.

The holder pushes the folded body along the floor and out of the open mouth. It stays in gel and water the whole way, so nothing is lifted; the push needs 1.8 N at the bath's yield stress of 9 Pa (arm: 4.9 N).

Outside, on the soft two lumen line: the pump pulls the gel out of the quilt while air pushes in behind it (6 serpentine loops, 4.2 min); the quilt fills to 13.6 kPa and the newborn opens to its printed shape; then 1613 mL of gel go back into the lowest cells as ballast.
The arm draws the line back; the valve closes. The newborn floats with its floor 4 mm over the tank floor: the gel in its lowest cells holds it down.
The newborn swims mouth first on its own pump: an arc to the left, across, an arc to the right into the free lane beside the old head, then the pump stops and it coasts to rest.
The cord motor in the tail tilts the three seam magnets off their keepers (12.8 N at each tab); the tail backs off 80 mm on its wheels.
The tail turns on the spot, drives into the free lane, turns back and drives up behind the newborn.
Nine magnet pairs in the tail face pull the steel disks in the cuff; the nipple on the face seats in the valve and feeds the interlayer from the tail's pump.
The line on the arm lays gel into the soft head from the floor up; the water above it leaves through the open mouth. With its lowest cells full of gel the soft head settles onto the tank floor.
Generation 2, in the soft head: the holder seats the next kit, exactly as in the hard head.
Tool change in the tail.
Cure in the gel of the soft head, then the holder.
The second newborn is born; the soft head stands as it stood, open, inflated, with its gel: it can give the next birth.

checks.name: With the fertile hard head (mouth 334 mm from the docking plane) the holder pushes the folded body at most to 247 mm from the plane: 89 mm short. An open interior gives no pressure to carry it the rest (the jet gives 0.039 N, the gel holds it with about 0.3 N or more).
New hard head, mouth 245 mm from the docking plane: the holder pushes the rear face of the folded body 5 mm past the mouth plane (reach 284 mm at 30 to 60 mm height, 5 mm kept in hand)

Roof against every arm move (unfold, kit, tool changes, the new print and push): smallest clearance 8.4 mm where 7.0 mm are needed (3 mm and 10 mm of crown drop at the roof, 3 mm and 4 mm of sway at the sides); the quilt sits outside the inner skin, which is the hard head's inner face
The print needle reaches every point of the folded body (210 sample points, official joint ranges); its head stays above the gel

Quilt laid flat (each cell lies flat pi r wide, so the flat quilt is pi / 2 longer than the shell), Z folded 3 across and 3 along; the creases along the body fall on the seams after cells 3 and 6: 128 x 187 x 79.2 mm, 18 layers, packing 0.61
The folded body passes the open mouth: 201 mm wide at the floor, 269 at its top, roof 286 mm; the body 187 wide, 79 tall
Gel bowl the full width of the head (no ledge in the section), gel 86.7 mm deep at the water level, 5.19 L in the hard head (fertile 3.14 L)
Even quilt in Dragon Skin 10 NV, cells r 8 mm: needs 36.7 kPa, allows 8.0 kPa (frame per meter of body, loads x 2, limit point / 1.5, gel ballast in the low cells)
Even quilt in Dragon Skin 10 NV, cells r 12 mm: needs 15.8 kPa, allows 5.3 kPa (frame per meter of body, loads x 2, limit point / 1.5, gel ballast in the low cells)
Even quilt in Dragon Skin 10 NV, cells r 16 mm: needs 8.7 kPa, allows 4.0 kPa (frame per meter of body, loads x 2, limit point / 1.5, gel ballast in the low cells)
Even quilt in Dragon Skin 30, cells r 8 mm: needs 36.3 kPa, allows 25.4 kPa (frame per meter of body, loads x 2, limit point / 1.5, gel ballast in the low cells)
Even quilt in Dragon Skin 30, cells r 12 mm: needs 15.7 kPa, allows 16.9 kPa (frame per meter of body, loads x 2, limit point / 1.5, gel ballast in the low cells)
Even quilt in Dragon Skin 30, cells r 16 mm: needs 8.6 kPa, allows 12.7 kPa (frame per meter of body, loads x 2, limit point / 1.5, gel ballast in the low cells)

Chosen: Dragon Skin 30, 9 hoop cells r 13.6 mm (27 mm deep, 27 mm pitch), one pressure 13.6 kPa (need 12.9 at the rim end, 8.6 at the mouth; allowed 14.9); hoop stretch 1.16; no tube stands out of the quilt

The lower lip is the front edge of the floor, on the tank floor. Gel and water stand level: 0.0 to 2.6 Pa of head at the open face against a yield stress of 9 Pa (density difference 0 to 3 kg/m3, estimate)
Clamp with the interior open: 16.7 N to hold; nine magnet pairs 172 to 343 N on steel disks in the cuff; the quilt carries the rim edge

Channel 9.8 m as 6 serpentine loops from the inlet manifold to the outlet manifold at the rim; gel in the flat channels 419 mL; plug push 0.16 / 0.44 / 0.88 kPa at 9 / 25 / 50 Pa, under 13.6 kPa; 4.2 min at 100 mL/min

Ballast is gel: 1613 mL in the cells below 68 mm (neutral in water, it only takes the place of air) leave 161 mL of air under the float line; the newborn (1.58 N in water) floats with its floor 4 mm over the tank floor
Push at 9 Pa yield: 1.7 / 1.8 / 2.0 N at friction 0.1 / 0.2 / 0.3 against 4.9 N (margin 2.5 x)
Push at 25 Pa yield: 4.3 / 4.5 / 4.6 N against 4.9 N (margin 1.06 x; the taller folded body has more surface in the gel)
Tail in 87 mm of water: about 2.6 N at the wheels (fertile 12 N)
Release: seam magnets tilt on hinged tabs, 12.8 N each (x 2 = 25.6) against one Pololu 298:1 gearmotor on a 5 mm spool, 39 N at half stall
Every pose inside the official joint ranges (3093 frames)
Per frame penetration test, every pair: worst 0.00 mm

verdict.why: The holder reaches 284 mm; the mouth stands 245 mm from the docking plane, open to the floor. Roof margin 1.4 mm over the allowances.
Quilt laid flat, Z folded 3 x 3 on its seams: 128 x 187 x 79 mm, packing 0.61; gel 5.19 L at 87 mm.

verdict.ok: fails in Dragon Skin 10 NV at any cell size; passes in Dragon Skin 30
verdict.why: An even quilt of 9 hoop cells r 13.6 mm at 13.6 kPa (allowed 14.9). In Dragon Skin 10 NV the full flat roofed section needs 9 to 66 kPa for cells r 16 to 6 mm, where the cells may take 4 to 11 kPa; deepening cells does not help at one pressure (capacity grows as r^2, the ballooning limit falls as 1/r).
Gel at the water level: open mouth, lip on the floor (estimate, bench test).
6 serpentine loops of 1.6 m: 0.16 to 0.88 kPa, 4.2 min; 5.7 L of air.

verdict.ok: passes; push margin 2.5 x at 9 Pa, 1.06 x at 25 Pa
verdict.why: Gel ballast 1613 mL in the lowest cells; push 1.7 to 2.0 N at 9 Pa, 4.3 to 4.6 N at 25 Pa, arm 4.9 N.

verdict.point: A soft head gives a birth
verdict.why: Interior open, never under pressure, gel level with the water, the hard head's inner face: the same moves print and push the next newborn.

limits: Bench test 1, quilt channel in Carbopol: a strip of 9 hoop cells, 27 mm pitch, printed flat with a 1 mm gel gap in Dragon Skin 30, cleared by suction and air through a two lumen needle; pass: no gel left, cells round, holds 13.6 kPa, limit point over 20 kPa.

Bench test 2, a full section of quilt (the head's section, 27 mm deep cells) at 13.6 kPa: crown drop under 10 mm, side sway under 4 mm, no wrinkle at twice the load; the 2D frame per meter used here ignores the shell's own stiffness along the body.
Bench test 3, folding the quilt: creases along the seams, and the creases across the cells at the pinch seams; pass: reopens without a leak.
Bench test 4, permeation of Dragon Skin 30 at 13.6 kPa in water; sizes the tail's pump and relief valve.
Bench test 5, open gel face: Carbopol 0.2 %% at the water level behind an open mouth for 24 h; pass: the face stands, under 5 %% of the gel lost.
Bench test 6, push: the folded body (79 mm tall) pushed 160 mm along the floor in gel with 4.9 N; the margin at 25 Pa yield is only 6 %.
Bench test 7, printing Dragon Skin 30 in Carbopol by the arm's needle (pot life 45 min, cure 16 h).
Bench test 8, release: a DC2-N52 seam magnet tilted off its keeper by a cord; pass: under 26 N.
Bench test 9, gel ballast: 1613 mL of gel pumped back into the lowest cells after clearing; does it stay there, and does the newborn float at 4 mm.
Not modeled: the unfolding is drawn as a direct morph from the folded body through the laid flat quilt to the final shape.
Not modeled: swim speed and turning radius are estimates (fertile build); drag of the open, flooded shell is estimated.

Estimates: gel density equal to water, gel yield stress 9 to 50 Pa, friction, the 1 mm gel gaps, the push as twice the yield stress on the folded body, the tail's buoyancy scaled from the fertile build, the cuff.
The tail must carry 1154 mL of silicone for each newborn (material is not a constraint for the artist; the bores are not designed here).

deriv.name: Mouth
deriv.why: The holder reaches 284 mm along the floor; the rear face of the folded body must pass the mouth by 5 mm.

deriv.name: Gel and water
deriv.why: Floor skin and seat bumps (4.5 mm), the folded quilt (79.2 mm), 3 mm of gel over it; water at the same level so the soft walls carry no gel pressure and the open mouth holds its gel.

deriv.name: Quilt
deriv.why: Nine cells put two seams on the two creases of the Z fold along the body; at this size Dragon Skin 30 holds the section at one pressure.

deriv.name: Pressure
deriv.why: The highest need along the body (at the rim end), with the load x 2, plus 5 %; under the limit point / 1.5 (14.9 kPa).

deriv.name: Gel ballast
deriv.why: Gel in the cells below 68 mm takes the place of air, so only 161 mL of air stays under the float line, which carries the newborn's 1.58 N in water.

deriv.name: Silicone
deriv.why: Shell 0.267 m2, quilted (pi times a skin), and the cuff.
